name: Ajay Relan
current_role: Managing Director, Sharda Motor Industries Ltd (New Delhi)
profile: Ajay Relan is Managing Director of Sharda Motor Industries, an Indian auto-components maker (exhaust/emission-control systems, suspension) founded by the Relan family. He oversees manufacturing, plants, R&D and product development; wealth is shared with family member Rohit Relan.
interesting_fact: Holds a B.Com (Hons.) and completed Harvard Business School's three-year Owner/President Management (OPM) programme.
deep_cut_fact: Company profile credits him with personally overseeing R&D and new-project set-ups across Sharda's plants, alongside completing HBS's Owner/President Management programme.
notes: Family-run listed company; best route is via company IR/contact page. Auto-components angle rather than energy/data centers (emissions tech).

name: Patrick Fleury
current_role: CFO & Treasurer, TeraWulf Inc. (WULF); Director, Corvex, Inc.
profile: Patrick Fleury has been CFO of TeraWulf, the bitcoin-mining-turned-AI/HPC data-center developer, since May 2022, leading its capital raising for expansion. He spent ~24 years in finance: Banc of America energy & power banking, MD at Blackstone's GSO Capital Partners, and founding member of Platinum Equity's credit team.
interesting_fact: Began his career in the Global Energy & Power Investment Banking Group at Banc of America Securities before moving into credit investing at Blackstone/GSO.
deep_cut_fact: Graduated magna cum laude from Bowdoin College with a BA in Economics and Government & Legal Studies.
notes: Highly relevant for energy/data-center podcast (TeraWulf's Lake Mariner / AI hosting deals). Regular conference speaker (SALT, RBLT) - conference circuit is a natural route.

name: Y Swetha
profile: Listed (~US$132m) with wealth from Medha Servo Drives, a privately held Hyderabad maker of rail propulsion/traction systems, signalling and, more recently, solar inverters and EV drives. No public source found identifying Y Swetha's role at the company; public director lists name other Yadavelli/Nookala family members.
interesting_fact: Medha Servo Drives (founded 1984, Hyderabad) supplies rail propulsion equipment to 50+ countries and has diversified into solar string inverters (250 kW unit launched at Intersolar India 2024).
notes: Identity/role could not be confirmed; likely a family shareholder of a private company with no public profile. Company itself is relevant (rail electrification, solar inverters). Approach via company only.

name: Mario A Harik
current_role: Chairman (since Dec 2025) and CEO, XPO, Inc.; Director, QXO, Inc.
profile: Mario Harik is chairman and CEO of XPO, the North American LTL trucking carrier. A founding executive of Brad Jacobs' XPO in 2011, he was CIO, built its tech platform, ran LTL from 2021 and became CEO in 2022 after the GXO/RXO spin-offs. He also sits on the board of Jacobs' QXO.
interesting_fact: As XPO's CIO he ran the technology integrations of 17 acquisitions in four years, then spent six years building digital tools for the Con-way LTL business he later took over.
deep_cut_fact: Engineer by training: computer & communications engineering from the American University of Beirut and an MIT master's in IT; early in his career he co-founded G3 Analyst as chief architect of web and voice applications, and was CTO of Tallan.
notes: Media contact Cole Horton listed on XPO press releases (mid-2026). Tech-heavy CEO (AI in freight ops) - good podcast angle; spoke at Northwestern in 2026.

name: Mahabir Prasad Jalan
current_role: Chairman Emeritus (founder), Ramkrishna Forgings Ltd, Kolkata
profile: Mahabir Prasad Jalan founded Ramkrishna Forgings in Kolkata in 1981, initially making forged parts for Indian Railways; the firm moved into commercial-vehicle components around 2000 and is now a major listed forging/casting exporter. He chaired it until 2023 and is now Chairman Emeritus, with son Naresh Jalan as MD and grandson Chaitanya Jalan in management.
interesting_fact: RKFL began in 1981 as a railway forging supplier and only entered the automotive market around 2000, later becoming a key supplier of heavy-truck components globally.
deep_cut_fact: Has said: 'Honesty, dedication, and customer engagement are the three cardinal mantras that RKFL believes in' - and blamed India's early forging struggles on outdated techniques and low volumes.
notes: Now semi-retired (emeritus); for a podcast the active family leaders (Naresh / Chaitanya Jalan) may be more accessible. Alive status inferred from 2025-26 board listings naming him Chairman Emeritus.

name: Nav Ratan Goenka
current_role: Chairman & Managing Director (founder), Diamond Beverages Pvt Ltd, Kolkata
profile: Nav Ratan Goenka founded Diamond Beverages, a Kolkata-based Coca-Cola franchise bottler incorporated in 1995 that bottles Coca-Cola soft drinks, Maaza, Minute Maid and Kinley water for eastern India. Registry records list him as a director since 1995; day-to-day leadership is with MD Hemant Goenka and director Abhyuday Goenka.
interesting_fact: Diamond Beverages is one of Coca-Cola's franchise bottlers in India, producing carbonated drinks, fruit beverages (Maaza, Minute Maid Pulpy Orange) and Kinley packaged water.
notes: Private family business with no public website found (diamondbeverages.in is parked). Not to be confused with Shiv Ratan Goenka of Bengal Beverages. Alive status not confirmed from a dated source.

name: Elizabeth P Bruno
current_role: Director, Brady Corporation (since 2003); President, Brady Education Foundation (Chapel Hill, NC)
profile: Dr. Elizabeth Pungello Bruno is a descendant of Brady Corp founder William H. Brady Jr. and a long-time Brady director, with the family holding control of the voting stock. A former developmental psychology researcher at UNC Chapel Hill, she leads the Brady Education Foundation, which funds research on closing educational opportunity gaps.
interesting_fact: Through the Brady Education Foundation she helped launch a roughly $3M initiative to rigorously study public Montessori education, with the Trust for Learning.
deep_cut_fact: A University of Rochester alumna (class of 1989) who has served on Rochester's board of trustees, and a former UNC developmental psychology faculty member before running the family foundation.
notes: Sources differ on whether she is the founder's granddaughter (Brady IR site) or great-granddaughter (BizTimes). Philanthropy/education-research focused; foundation contact form is the best route. Brady IR contact Ann Thornton by phone only.

name: Mauad Bruno Sousa
current_role: Partner & equities portfolio manager, Kapitalo Investimentos (Sao Paulo); Independent Director, Aura Minerals (AUGO) since 2020
profile: Bruno Sousa Mauad is a Brazilian investor - partner in charge of equities strategies at Sao Paulo hedge fund Kapitalo Investimentos (executive committee since 2019) - and an independent director of gold/copper miner Aura Minerals. His SEC-reported holdings largely reflect Kapitalo-managed Aura shares. Earlier he was at Ashmore Brasil and Patria Investimentos.
interesting_fact: Started his career at Patria Investimentos in 2005, later a senior PM at Ashmore Brasil before joining Kapitalo in 2015.
deep_cut_fact: Public Administration graduate of FGV-EAESP (Sao Paulo) and a CFA charterholder.
notes: Low public profile; bio facts are from aggregator (MarketScreener) rather than primary filings. Route via Aura IR or Kapitalo.

name: Charles Lynn Hamilton
current_role: Chief Site Development Officer, Fermi Inc. (Fermi America, NASDAQ/LSE: FRMI)
profile: Charles 'Charlie' Hamilton is Chief Site Development Officer of Fermi America, which is building Project Matador, a nuclear/gas-powered 'HyperGrid' AI data-center campus in the Texas Panhandle near Amarillo. He leads site development and has testified to the Texas House on the campus's water strategy; his wealth stems from Fermi insider shares.
interesting_fact: In June 2026 he told the Texas House Natural Resources Committee that Project Matador's four-pillar water strategy (dry/hybrid cooling, closed-loop reuse) would use ~80% less water than conventional data-center cooling.
deep_cut_fact: A sixth-generation Texan who grew up on a cow-calf and peanut farm; his family has worked the Panhandle for more than 130 years.
notes: Goes by Charlie Hamilton. Highly on-topic (AI power campus, nuclear, water). Fermi has had executive turnover (CEO/CFO departures, interim CFO) in 2026. Earlier career not verified (search budget exhausted).

name: Navdeep S Sooch
current_role: Co-founder and Chairman of the Board, Silicon Laboratories (Silicon Labs), Austin, TX
profile: Nav Sooch co-founded Austin chipmaker Silicon Labs in 1996 with fellow Crystal Semiconductor alumni Dave Welland and Jeff Scott, was CEO until 2003 (and interim CEO in 2005) and has chaired the board since inception. From 2011-2018 he was CEO of Ketra, a solid-state lighting startup. Earlier he was VP Engineering at Crystal Semiconductor/Cirrus Logic and a design engineer at AT&T Bell Labs.
interesting_fact: Silicon Labs' first product (1998), a cheaper, smaller silicon DAA modem chip, took sales from $5.6M in 1998 to nearly $47M in 1999; the company also built the first CMOS RF synthesizer for mobile phones.
deep_cut_fact: Holds a B.S. in Electrical Engineering from the University of Michigan-Dearborn and an M.S. from Stanford, and started out as a design engineer at AT&T Bell Labs before Crystal Semiconductor.
notes: Serial founder (Silicon Labs, Ketra lighting) - strong entrepreneurship angle. No published personal contact found; route via Silicon Labs corporate communications / IR.
